rule: Crop the largest rectangle (host) as the canvas; paste each smaller two-colour rectangle onto it in descending bounding-box area order, at the offset maximising +1 per agreeing and -1 per disagreeing cell, counted only over canvas cells whose colour is one of the piece's colours.
scope: Assemble separated rectangular pieces onto the largest slab, descending by area, using unique signed colour matches. Native separated/nested footprints, two-colour keys and mismatch-sensitive decoys.
constraints: Rejection retries preserve the initially sampled piece count; default one-piece frequency changed from 400/1000 to 162/1000, four-piece from 25/1000 to 165/1000 on the same seed range.

authored_scope: Random mode: grid 18..30 per side (30x30 favoured; non-30 sizes are synthetic extensions), host 5..15 x 5..17, 1-4 pasted pieces up to 9x9, sampled background/fill/key/hidden colours, block/line/ring/single-key patterns, shared key colours as distractors, hidden colour occasionally equal to another key or to the host fill, optional nested mode (pair-3 style) and decoy mode (no-penalty solver would fail). Explicit mode reconstructs fixtures and accepts arbitrary validated scenes 1..30 per side. Not supported: partially overlapping non-nested paste footprints, pieces with more than two colours, more than four pieces.
authored_constraints: Background is the strictly most frequent colour
All input pieces and host keep a one-cell gap (no 4- or 8-connectivity between objects)
Piece bounding-box areas are distinct and strictly below the host area, so paste order is unambiguous
Every intended paste offset is the unique maximum of the +/-1 score at its step
Piece keys differ from host fill; no piece uses the background colour
Each piece uses exactly two colours (key and hidden)
Non-nested paste footprints are disjoint with a gap inside the host; a nested piece is fully contained in its parent
Integer controls must be genuine ints (bools/floats rejected); nested/decoy must be None or bool
